decisions.reason: The original Definition asserted regular-value independence while allowing k=0. For a constant point-to-S^0 map both values are regular, with fibres point and empty; a compact neat codimension-zero cobordism in I is clopen and cannot have only its zero endpoint. Restricted only the independence clause to k>=1, retaining the rank-zero differential construction and explaining its exception. The normal-quotient isomorphism is exactly clauses (i), (ii), (iv) of the transverse-preimage supplier.

F8 attributes reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity to a definition that expressly defers them. Replaced that citation by lem-framed-cobordism-is-an-equivalence-relation and added its direct dependency, supplying the quotient-class construction. Checked its product cylinder, reflected normal quotient and matching product-end gluing proof. All inverse-map and smooth-representative arguments use n>=k>=1, so the corrected regular-preimage Definition retains every application; the theorem Statement is unchanged.

The Example and conclusion incorrectly said that choice enters only through the bundle lifting theorem. F1, F2 and F7 also inherit AC_omega from the regular-preimage, collapse and PT suppliers. Full AC already implies this, so the generator claim is sound and this is nonfatal assumption accounting. Both passages now state these uses and the countable-choice dependency is explicit. Checked the affine rank-two differential, finite support-subordinate partition, vanishing outer circle homotopy groups, exact-sequence isomorphism and identity degree +1.

Original F3 omitted the degree supplier's connectedness hypothesis; disconnected target components can have different signed sums (degrees 1 and 2 on two sphere components). This is a nonfatal overstatement because every actual application is S^n to S^n with n>=1. F3 now requires nonempty connected manifolds. Step 2.1 explicitly supplies global smoothness of the normalized finite collapse, properness, connected oriented spheres, and the empty regular fibre. The signed-count classification and Example are unchanged.
